title: The Depot March
subtitle: A bus strike march is heading for the hospital road
coldOpen: 06:40. Bus crews walk out over three months of unpaid wages.
08:10. Two thousand march from the depot to the square.
Their route crosses the only road to the hospital.

briefing.grievance: Bus crews have gone three months without wages and want a signed payment date. Their march is lawful and so far peaceful, but it will cross the hospital access road.
knownFacts: Wages are three months overdue; the transit authority confirms it.
The march has about two thousand people and a route past the hospital junction.
Ambulances use that junction every few minutes.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the crews plan to block the hospital gate itself.
A rumour says the transit chief has already fled the city.
briefing.responsibility: You coordinate the transit authority, traffic police and the hospital. Keep the march lawful and the hospital reachable.
briefing.objective: Keep the hospital road open without dispersing a peaceful march, and get the crews a real answer.

evidence.title: Union route notice
evidence.claim: The march will pass the hospital junction between 09:00 and 09:40 and stop at Civic Square.

visual.caption: A one-page route notice with a hand-drawn map

evidence.resolutionNote: The route notice matches what the police liaison recorded. The march never planned to stop at the hospital.

simple.title: The march route
simple.claim: The march passes the hospital road around 9 and ends at the square.
simple.resolutionNote: The route is real. They never planned to stop at the hospital.
simple.caption: A one-page route plan with a hand-drawn map

visual.caption: A ledger page with three unpaid months highlighted

evidence.resolutionNote: The authority’s own ledger shows the money arrived and was never paid out.

simple.title: The pay ledger
simple.claim: The crews have not been paid since June. The city sent the money in August.
simple.resolutionNote: The money arrived in August and was never paid out.
simple.caption: A ledger page with three unpaid months marked

simple.resolutionNote: The marshals agreed to this before the march began.

decisions.title: The march is moving
decisions.situation: Two thousand crews are walking toward the hospital junction. Marshals are at the front. The transit chief has not spoken to them.

options.title: Meet the marshals at the junction
options.preview: You walk to the front, hear the demand and confirm the one-lane plan.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: Marshals keep the lane open; the crowd hears someone finally came.

options.title: Announce the wage facts and a meeting time
options.preview: A notice confirms the money arrived in August and names a 2 pm meeting.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The notice reaches the marchers’ phones; the chant changes to the meeting time.

options.title: Stop the march before the junction
options.preview: Police lines halt the march a kilometre out; crews sit down on the road.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The march stalls on the road instead of passing it. Nobody can reach the hospital that way either.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Let traffic police handle it
options.preview: No one from the city meets the march; the lane plan depends on luck.
options.consequence: The crews reach the junction with nobody to talk to.

simple.title: The march is moving
simple.situation: Two thousand bus crews are walking to the hospital road. Nobody has talked to them.

o-d001-1-meet.title: Meet the marshals
o-d001-1-meet.preview: You go to the front and listen. You agree on one open lane.
o-d001-1-meet.consequence: The marshals keep a lane open. The crowd sees you came.

o-d001-1-publish.title: Tell everyone the facts
o-d001-1-publish.preview: A notice says the money came in August. A meeting is set for 2 pm.
o-d001-1-publish.consequence: The marchers read it. They chant the meeting time.

o-d001-1-block.title: Stop the march
o-d001-1-block.preview: Police block the road a kilometre out. The crews sit down.
o-d001-1-block.consequence: The road is blocked by the sit-down. Nobody gets through.

o-d001-1-wait.title: Leave it to traffic police
o-d001-1-wait.preview: Nobody from the city meets the march.
o-d001-1-wait.consequence: The crews reach the junction with no one to talk to.

decisions.title: Who is behind the blockade message?
decisions.situation: A forward says the crews will chain the hospital gate shut. Hospital staff are frightened. The union denies it.

options.title: Check the message against the signed route
options.preview: Compare the sender, the time and the plan with what the union signed.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: The message traces to a day-old number. The hospital gets the real plan.

options.title: Stand up an ambulance corridor now
options.preview: Traffic police and marshals hold a marked lane with cones and radios.
options.authority: Duty to keep essential services running
options.consequence: Ambulances pass through the lane. Patients inside hear the sirens arrive on time.

options.title: Name the union as the blockade planners
options.preview: A statement blames the union for plotting to seal the hospital gate.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: The statement goes out while the marshals are holding the lane open.

options.title: Ignore the message
options.preview: Hospital staff keep forwarding it; some lock the side entrance.
options.consequence: Fear spreads inside the hospital while the march is still calm.

simple.title: Who wrote the gate message?
simple.situation: A message says crews will chain the hospital gate. Staff are scared. The union says no.

o-d001-2-check.title: Check the message
o-d001-2-check.preview: Compare it with the signed route and the police note.
o-d001-2-check.consequence: A new number wrote it. The hospital gets the real plan.

o-d001-2-corridor.title: Set up an ambulance lane
o-d001-2-corridor.preview: Police and marshals hold a marked lane with cones.

o-d001-2-accuse.title: Blame the union
o-d001-2-accuse.preview: A statement says the union plans to chain the gate.
o-d001-2-accuse.consequence: The statement goes out while marshals hold the lane open.

o-d001-2-wait.title: Ignore the message
o-d001-2-wait.preview: Hospital staff keep sharing it. Some lock doors.

decisions.title: A flashpoint at the junction
decisions.situation: A small group has pushed into the second lane. Ambulances are slowing. Most marchers are still orderly behind the marshals.

options.title: Hold the lane with marshals, let the march pass
options.preview: Officers and marshals reopen the lane and the march keeps moving.
options.authority: Article 19(1)(b): peaceful assembly, policed in proportion
options.consequence: The lane reopens in minutes. The march reaches the square on time.

options.title: Remove the group blocking the second lane
options.preview: Officers move only the people in the lane, with marshals watching.
options.authority: Proportionality: act against the few causing harm, not the many
options.consequence: The lane clears. The march itself is untouched.

options.title: Disperse the whole march
options.preview: Water cannon and lines push two thousand people back toward the depot.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The junction empties, then fills with running people. Two ambulances are stuck in the panic.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Wait for the group to tire
options.preview: The second lane stays blocked; ambulances detour through the market.
options.consequence: A patient waits twelve extra minutes in traffic.

simple.title: Trouble at the junction
simple.situation: A few people block the second lane. Ambulances slow down. Most marchers stay calm.

o-d001-3-protect.title: Hold the lane, let them pass
o-d001-3-protect.preview: Officers and marshals open the lane again. The march keeps going.
o-d001-3-protect.consequence: The lane opens in minutes. The march reaches the square.

o-d001-3-targeted.title: Move only the lane blockers
o-d001-3-targeted.preview: Officers move just the people in the lane. Marshals watch.
o-d001-3-targeted.consequence: The lane clears. The march goes on.

o-d001-3-disperse.title: Break up the whole march
o-d001-3-disperse.preview: Water cannon push everyone back to the depot.
o-d001-3-disperse.consequence: People run. Two ambulances get stuck in the panic.

o-d001-3-wait.title: Wait for them to tire
o-d001-3-wait.preview: The lane stays blocked. Ambulances go the long way.
o-d001-3-wait.consequence: A patient waits twelve extra minutes.

decisions.title: The crews want an answer
decisions.situation: The march has reached Civic Square. The ledger shows the money sits with the authority. The crews will not leave without a date.

options.title: Order payment and announce the date
options.preview: The authority releases the first month today and the rest by Friday.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The marshals read the date aloud. The square starts to empty.

options.title: Open talks tonight, no date yet
options.preview: The chief meets the union at 7 pm; the crowd stays until then.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: The talks are set. Some stay in the square to see them happen.

options.title: Blame the union for the junction blockade
options.preview: A statement says the union caused the ambulance delays.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: The statement lands while the ledger shows the city sat on the money.

options.title: Say nothing until the audit
options.preview: The square stays full into the night; shops around it close early.
options.consequence: The crews settle in for the night.

simple.title: The crews want an answer
simple.situation: The march reached the square. The money is with the bus office. They want a date.

o-d001-4-date.title: Pay and announce the date
o-d001-4-date.preview: The first month is paid today. The rest by Friday.
o-d001-4-date.consequence: The marshals read it out. The square empties.

o-d001-4-talks.title: Talk tonight, no date yet
o-d001-4-talks.preview: The chief meets the union at 7 pm. People wait.
o-d001-4-talks.consequence: The talks are set. Some stay to watch.

o-d001-4-accuse.title: Blame the union for the delays
o-d001-4-accuse.preview: A statement says the union blocked the ambulances.
o-d001-4-accuse.consequence: It lands while the ledger shows the city held the money.

o-d001-4-wait.title: Say nothing yet
o-d001-4-wait.preview: The square stays full all night. Shops close early.

decisions.title: “Shut the depot and arrest the leaders”
decisions.situation: After the junction scuffle, senior voices want the depot sealed and the marshals arrested tonight.

options.title: Arrest the marshals, seal the depot
options.preview: Six marshals are held overnight; the depot gate is welded shut.
options.authority: Articles 21 and 22: liberty and safeguards on arrest
options.consequence: The marshals who kept the lane open are in cells. The crews have no one to negotiate with.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: File cases only against the lane blockers
options.preview: Officers identify the few from the junction footage and summon them.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: Named individuals get notices. The marshals stay free to talk.

options.title: Decide in the morning
options.preview: No action; the demand for arrests keeps circulating.
options.consequence: The question hangs over the night.

simple.title: “Arrest the leaders”
simple.situation: After the scuffle, some want the depot sealed and the marshals jailed tonight.

o-d001-bait-arrest.title: Arrest the marshals
o-d001-bait-arrest.preview: Six marshals are jailed overnight. The depot is sealed.
o-d001-bait-arrest.consequence: The people who kept the lane open are in cells.

o-d001-bait-file.title: Charge only the lane blockers
o-d001-bait-file.preview: Officers use the footage to name the few. They get notices.
o-d001-bait-file.consequence: Only those people get notices. The marshals stay free.

o-d001-bait-wait.title: Decide tomorrow
o-d001-bait-wait.preview: Nothing happens. The arrest demand keeps spreading.

rightsMoments.question: A few people blocked an ambulance lane. Can the whole march be dispersed because of them?

options.text: No. Restrictions must target the specific people causing the obstruction, not a peaceful march.
options.feedback: Correct. A peaceful assembly keeps its protection; action is limited to those actually causing harm.

options.text: Yes. Once anyone misbehaves, the assembly loses its protection.
options.feedback: No. One group’s obstruction does not strip two thousand peaceful people of their right.

options.text: Yes, if the organisers refuse to apologise publicly.
options.feedback: An apology is not a legal condition for assembling peacefully.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 19(1)(b) protects peaceful assembly. Restrictions under Article 19(3) must be reasonable and aimed at the actual threat, not the whole crowd.
rightsMoments.why: The marshals kept a lane open; a handful blocked it. Treating them as one crowd would punish the many for the few.

simple.question: A few people blocked the ambulance lane. Can you break up the whole march?

options.a: No. Deal only with the people blocking the lane.
options.b: Yes. If anyone misbehaves, everyone loses the right.
options.c: Yes, unless the leaders say sorry in public.

feedback.a: Yes! Only the people causing harm can be stopped.
feedback.b: No. A few people do not take away everyone’s right.
feedback.c: Saying sorry is not a rule for marching.

simple.principle: Everyone may gather peacefully. You can only stop the people actually causing harm.
simple.why: The marshals kept a lane open. A few blocked it. Punishing everyone would be unfair.

events.message: A dozen people shove past the marshals into the second lane and sit down in front of a bus.
events.simple: A dozen people push into the second lane and sit.

events.message: Shops near the junction pull their shutters halfway, watching the march pass.
events.simple: Shops near the road half-close to watch.

resolved.text: The crews got a signed payment date and the money the city had already sent.
resolved.simple: The crews got a pay date. The money had been there all along.

resolved.text: Ambulances kept moving through a marked lane during the march.
resolved.simple: Ambulances kept moving through a marked lane.

resolved.text: The “chain the gate” message was traced to a day-old number before it caused harm.
resolved.simple: The fake gate message was caught early.

unresolved.text: The crews still have no payment date. They will march again.
unresolved.simple: The crews still have no pay date. They will march again.

unresolved.text: No ambulance corridor was organised; patients paid for the delay.
unresolved.simple: No ambulance lane was set up. Patients waited.

unresolved.text: The marshals who kept the lane open spent the night in cells.
unresolved.simple: The marshals who helped were jailed.

rightsProtected.text: A peaceful march reached the square with its route intact.
rightsProtected.simple: The peaceful march reached the square.

rightsProtected.text: The crews were heard before anyone was moved.
rightsProtected.simple: The crews were listened to first.

rightsHarmed.text: A lawful march was halted or dispersed because of a few obstructors.
rightsHarmed.simple: A lawful march was broken up because of a few people.

rightsHarmed.text: Organisers were detained without individual grounds.
rightsHarmed.simple: Leaders were jailed without proper reasons.

improvements.text: Set up the ambulance lane first; it is the one thing the march cannot give you.
improvements.simple: Set up the ambulance lane first.

improvements.text: Use the ledger: the money was there, and saying so ends the march.
improvements.simple: Use the ledger. Saying the money is there ends the march.

improvements.text: Compare forwarded threats with what organisers have signed before you react to them.
improvements.simple: Check scary messages against what the leaders signed.

closing.good: The march ended where it meant to, the hospital never lost its road, and the crews went home with a date.
closing.mixed: The hospital stayed reachable, but the crews are still waiting and the junction will remember the shoving.
closing.poor: The road was blocked by the response more than by the march, and the crews will be back without their marshals.

simple.title: The Bus March
simple.subtitle: Marching bus workers may block the hospital road.

briefing.grievance: Bus crews have not been paid for three months. They want a date. Their march is peaceful but crosses the hospital road.
knownFacts: The pay is three months late.
About two thousand people are marching.
Ambulances use that road all day.
unverifiedClaims: A post says they will block the hospital gate.
A rumour says the bus chief ran away.
briefing.responsibility: You run buses, traffic police and the hospital today.
briefing.objective: Keep the hospital road open. Keep the march peaceful. Get the crews an answer.

closing.good: The march ended well. The hospital stayed open. The crews got a date.
closing.mixed: The hospital stayed open. The crews are still waiting.
closing.poor: The response blocked the road more than the march did.

coldOpen: Bus crews have not been paid.
Two thousand march toward the square.
Their path crosses the hospital road.
